html[1]/body[1]/header[1]/div[1]/div[1]/.text: Your Basis switchboard measures every circuit in your home. Corrente adds your solar and battery on top of that: it shares the solar you generated and the battery you discharged across those circuits, in proportion to what each one was drawing at the time. That step provides a more realistic estimate of what each circuit costs to run.

That step provides a more realistic estimate of what each circuit costs to run.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.text: The problem
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.was: The problem

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.text: Solar usually isn't allocated per circuit
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.was: Solar usually isn't allocated per circuit

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.text: Unless your solar is wired to its own sub-circuit, your panels feed the whole house at once — so the switchboard allocates every kilowatt-hour to grid usage at your plan's time-of-use rates, as if it had all been imported.
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.was: Unless your solar is wired to its own sub-circuit, your panels feed the whole house at once — so the switchboard allocates every kilowatt-hour to grid usage at your plan's time-of-use rates, as if it had all been imported.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.was: Proportional allocation

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.text: Solar and battery, allocated in proportion
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.was: Solar and battery, allocated in proportion

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.text: For every interval of the day, Corrente works out how much of the home's total load your own generation covered, then gives each circuit that same share, weighted by what the circuit actually drew. A circuit pulling a third of the load at midday gets a third of the solar.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.was: Amortised solar & battery

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.text: The amortised cost of solar and battery
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.was: The amortised cost of solar and battery

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.text: Corrente lets you enter your own amortised cost per kWh for solar and battery, calculated however you like — for example, install cost (plus a replacement inverter, since they typically only last around 10 years) divided by expected generation over a 20-year lifespan. That gives an honest running cost instead of treating self-generated energy as free.
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.was: Corrente lets you enter your own amortised cost per kWh for solar and battery, calculated however you like — for example, install cost (plus a replacement inverter, since they typically only last around 10 years) divided by expected generation over a 20-year lifespan. That gives an honest running cost instead of treating self-generated energy as free.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.text: Two numbers that matter
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.was: Two numbers that matter

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.text: Estimated bill cost and savings, per circuit
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.was: Estimated bill cost and savings, per circuit

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[1]/div[1.text: Bill Cost is what your retailer will actually charge for that circuit — only the kWh that came from the grid, at your plan's own peak, shoulder, and off-peak rates. Savings is what you avoided paying by running on your own generation instead. Together they tell you what a circuit costs and what your system is doing for it.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[2]/div[1.text:
Basis Home — cost by rate band

Every hour the circuit ran, priced against the grid tariff in force at the time. Total for the day: $8.55 — the right answer to "what would this have cost from the grid?", but it can't correctly allocate solar generation unless solar is wired to its own circuit.
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[2]/div[1.was:
Basis Home — cost by rate band

Every hour the circuit ran, priced against the grid tariff in force at the time. Total for the day: $8.55 — the right answer to "what would this have cost from the grid?", but it can't correctly allocate solar generation unless solar is wired to its own circuit.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[2]/div[1.was: Corrente's chart for the same circuit and day: overnight bars in off-peak blue, midday bars in solar amber with a slice of battery magenta.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/section[2]/div[1.text:
Corrente — cost by source

The same day with your own generation accounted for. Corrente splits that $8.55 into $4.96 you'll actually be billed and $3.58 your solar and battery covered.

Corrente — cost by source

The same day with your own generation accounted for. Corrente splits that $8.55 into $4.96 you'll actually be billed and $3.58 your solar and battery covered.

html[1]/head[1]/meta[3]@content.text: Corrente is an iOS app for whole-home energy — built by Ant G, an ex-Wahooligan, to give one honest view of what your energy costs.
html[1]/head[1]/meta[3]@content.was: Corrente is an iOS app for whole-home energy — built by Ant G, an ex-Wahooligan, to give one honest view of what your energy costs.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/p[1].text: Corrente is developed by Ant G, an ex-Wahooligan who helped build the Wahoo ELEMNT iOS Companion app. Corrente grew out of wanting one honest view of a home's energy — where it's generated, where it's stored, and what it actually costs.
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/p[1].was: Corrente is developed by Ant G, an ex-Wahooligan who helped build the Wahoo ELEMNT iOS Companion app. Corrente grew out of wanting one honest view of a home's energy — where it's generated, where it's stored, and what it actually costs.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/p[2].text: Corrente is Italian for current — the flow of electricity, and of energy through your home.
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/p[2].was: Corrente is Italian for current — the flow of electricity, and of energy through your home.

html[1]/head[1]/meta[3]@content.text: How Corrente handles your energy data, account, and connected-service credentials — no advertising, no data selling.
html[1]/head[1]/meta[3]@content.was: How Corrente handles your energy data, account, and connected-service credentials — no advertising, no data selling.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.text: Using Corrente's cloud features requires a Corrente account, identified by your email address. Beyond that, Corrente does not collect personal information, and it never sells your data or uses it for advertising.
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.was: Using Corrente's cloud features requires a Corrente account, identified by your email address. Beyond that, Corrente does not collect personal information, and it never sells your data or uses it for advertising.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.text: Corrente reads energy data — such as solar generation, battery state of charge, grid import and export, and home consumption — from the energy systems you choose to connect, including Tesla Powerwall and a Basis switchboard.
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.was: Corrente reads energy data — such as solar generation, battery state of charge, grid import and export, and home consumption — from the energy systems you choose to connect, including Tesla Powerwall and a Basis switchboard.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.text: To do this you authorise Corrente with each service using that service's own sign-in. Corrente only reads the data those services expose for your own systems.
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.was: To do this you authorise Corrente with each service using that service's own sign-in. Corrente only reads the data those services expose for your own systems.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.text: The OAuth tokens and API keys used to reach your energy services are stored in your device's Keychain. When you sign in to a Corrente account, they are also synced to CorrenteServer so it can fetch your energy data on your behalf. They are only ever used to talk to the services you connected.
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.was: The OAuth tokens and API keys used to reach your energy services are stored in your device's Keychain. When you sign in to a Corrente account, they are also synced to CorrenteServer so it can fetch your energy data on your behalf. They are only ever used to talk to the services you connected.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.text: Your energy data is used only to display your live status, history, costs, and ROI inside the app. It is not used for advertising or analytics.
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.was: Your energy data is used only to display your live status, history, costs, and ROI inside the app. It is not used for advertising or analytics.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.text: Corrente's cloud features are provided by CorrenteServer, a service operated by Corrente's developer. It fetches from your energy providers and stores your energy data — such as daily cost snapshots, circuit history, and your retail plan — so your history stays available without repeatedly querying those services.
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.was: Corrente's cloud features are provided by CorrenteServer, a service operated by Corrente's developer. It fetches from your energy providers and stores your energy data — such as daily cost snapshots, circuit history, and your retail plan — so your history stays available without repeatedly querying those services.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.text: This stored energy data is anonymised: it is associated only with your Corrente account, and is not linked to any other personal identifying information.
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.was: This stored energy data is anonymised: it is associated only with your Corrente account, and is not linked to any other personal identifying information.

html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.text: Corrente shares your requests only with the energy services you have connected, in order to fetch your own data. Nothing is shared with any other third party.
html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/article[1]/secti.was: Corrente shares your requests only with the energy services you have connected, in order to fetch your own data. Nothing is shared with any other third party.
